summary.one_liner: Grav is a fast, file-based (flat-file) web platform and CMS that needs no database and is set up by extracting a ZIP or using Composer or Git.
summary.what_it_does: Grav is a flat-file content management system where pages are stored as files rather than in a database. The README describes zero installation: extract the ZIP archive and it runs. It includes a Grav Package Manager (GPM) for installing, upgrading, and updating plugins, themes, and Grav itself from the command line. The core is built on Twig templates, Markdown and YAML content/config, Parsedown for Markdown Extra, Symfony Cache, Symfony Event Dispatcher and Console, Pimple dependency injection, and the Gregwar Image Library for dynamic image manipulation. A Symfony-based CLI (bin/grav) handles install tasks, and the project includes PHPUnit and PHPStan test commands for development. Full documentation is hosted at learn.getgrav.org.
use_cases: build a website without a database
publish blog posts or pages from Markdown files
run a flat-file CMS on a PHP web server
install and update CMS plugins and themes from the command line
customise site layouts with Twig templates
how_to_run: git clone the Grav repository into ~/webroot and cd into ~/webroot/grav
notable: No database or installation step; extract the ZIP and it runs
Grav Package Manager (GPM) for plugins, themes, and self-upgrades
Dedicated migration path for Grav 1.x to 2.0
caveats: Requires PHP 8.3 or higher, plus Apache or IIS configuration per the README
Upgrading from Grav 1.x to 2.0 needs a dedicated migration; bin/gpm selfupgrade alone does not cross that boundary
The README does not state a license name; it only refers to a LICENSE file
